1. Start Shizuku and allow access.
2. Open Recommended and select apps you do not use.
3. Test first, then choose Disable.
4. Use Backups & restore if you change your mind.
A test checks access and backups. It cannot predict whether you will miss an app or whether a phone feature will break.
App descriptions, source warnings and technical logs may remain in English. Read them before making changes.
Start with Recommended. Review, test, then disable apps you do not use.

For full app sizes, allow Usage access with Shizuku or in system settings. Until then, only APK sizes are shown.
Install Shizuku, then start it with Wireless debugging (Android 11+) or with root. No PC needed.
Open Shizuku and tap Start (Wireless debugging or root). It has to be started again after every reboot unless you have root.

Android Debloat List: %4$d
System App Remover: %5$d
Unlocks Expert, Unsafe and unlisted system apps. Protected core packages stay locked.
Preselects Delete app data when removing apps. This permanently deletes data. Leave off to keep data and settings (recommended).
Before disabling or removing, Debloater saves a restore point and verified APK copies. App data is not backed up. Choose Keep app data if you might want it back.
Using the lists built into this version of the app.
Download newer lists automatically when the app opens, at most once a week.
When lists disagree, the most cautious rating is used.

License: GPL-3.0. Includes the Universal Android Debloater Next Generation list (GPL-3.0, github.com/Universal-Debloater-Alliance) and overrides from System App Remover by santhosh-D-subramani (GPL-3.0), and the Android Debloat List by Muntashir Al-Islam (AGPL-3.0, adl.muntashir.dev). See NOTICE.md in the source code.
Supports Android 11 to 17 through Shizuku (ADB or root). Commands used: pm disable-user, pm enable, pm uninstall -k --user, cmd package install-existing, pm install-create/write/commit.

Download about 3 MB from GitHub: UAD-NG, Android Debloat List, System App Remover and Debloater’s own list (when public). Nothing is uploaded. Lists are checked before use; failed sources keep their previous version. You can return to built-in lists at any time. This updates ratings only.
Unsafe packages can break calls, Wi-Fi, notifications or cause a boot loop. Always run a test first and prefer Disable over Remove. If the phone fails to boot, only a factory reset may fix it.
Every tier together: each app shows its tier (Recommended, Safe, Extreme…). Read the warnings on Extreme and higher before removing.
No matching apps. Try another filter or search.
Bloatware, ads, telemetry, duplicates and apps you can get back from a store. Recommended for almost everyone; check you have another app for anything you use (browser, gallery…).
Safe to remove: the system is not affected, but these are apps you might still use (for example YouTube, Maps or Gmail).
Extreme debloat. These can break features such as notifications, payments, updates, the camera or calls. Read every warning, and run a test first.
Expert mode: packages that can break important features (rated Expert by UAD-NG). Prefer Disable, and test first.
Expert mode: critical packages. Removing them can cause boot loops or a non-working phone. Disable rather than remove, and test first.
Expert mode: system apps that are not in the debloat list. Their effect is unknown.
Selecting everything includes higher-risk apps. Read the warnings and test first.
Nothing will be changed. The test checks Shizuku access, packages, backups and free space. It cannot predict every effect on phone features.
A restore point and verified APK copies are saved first. Apps that cannot be backed up are skipped. App data is not backed up.
Apps are uninstalled for your user. System apps can be restored; user apps are reinstalled from their APK backup. Deleted data cannot be recovered.
Frees about %1$s. Data is permanently deleted and cannot be restored. Only APK files are backed up.
Estimated space freed: %1$s (data sizes may be incomplete)
Apps that may resist removal: %1$d (%2$s). If removal fails, retry with Disable.
Other packages need this app: %1$d. See details.
Safe to just get rid of
Might not be safe to remove
This screen shows ADL’s rating. Other screens combine all lists and use the most cautious rating.
A restore point and verified APK copies are saved before disabling or removing apps. Apps that cannot be backed up are skipped. App data is not backed up.
Backups are deleted if you uninstall Debloater. Export them to keep a copy.
Returns apps to the state saved when Debloater first ran. Enables disabled apps and reinstalls removed apps. Deleted app data cannot be recovered.
No backups yet. One is created automatically the first time you disable or remove an app.
Delete restore point and APK copies for %1$s? Removed user apps may no longer be restorable. System apps can still be restored from App manager.
TEST MODE: the process is simulated and checked, and nothing on your device is changed.
Backup: %1$s. Open Backups & restore to undo changes.
Nothing to restore in this selection
Everything already matches the original state
Bundled with the app; updated through APK releases. ADL and UAD update separately.
Clear temporary caches of installed user apps. App data and accounts are kept.
Select preinstalled app caches to free device storage. This does not change the read-only system partition.
Current Android user only. Shared caches are counted once. Other users and protected OS/recovery caches are outside this scan. Unknown sizes are excluded from totals.
Enable Usage access for Debloater, return here and scan again to measure other apps.
Connect Shizuku from Home before clearing caches. Scanning only needs Usage access.
This Android version does not advertise cache-only clearing. Nothing is cleared. Use each app’s Storage settings to clear its cache manually.
Filter by app or package name
Filtering does not deselect hidden apps.
Shared cache group. All listed apps are selected together.

Delete temporary caches only. App data and accounts are kept. Cache deletion cannot be undone or restored from debloat backups. Apps may rebuild caches and open more slowly next time. Measured cache: %1$s; actual space freed may differ.
Scan complete. %1$d cache group(s) could not be measured.
Cache clear: %1$d successful, %2$d failed. Sizes rescanned; running apps may rebuild caches immediately.
Cache clear: %1$d successful, %2$d failed. Rescan failed: %3$s. Scan again to refresh sizes.
No recommended apps are active on this phone. Want to go further? Open \"Debloat\" on the home screen.
Bloatware you can safely turn off: %1$d apps (%2$s).
These apps are bloatware, ads or tracking that most people never use. Turning them off is safe and can be undone at any time from \"Backups & restore\".
Nothing left to clean up. Your phone is already tidy.
Connect Shizuku first (see the home screen) to turn apps off. You can still look around.
Tip: \"Disable\" is the safest choice. The app stays on the phone but cannot run, show ads or track you.

Disable: the app stays on the phone but can\'t run. Safest, and fully reversible, but frees no space.\nRemove: the app is uninstalled for you. With \"Keep app data\" it can come back exactly as it was; with \"Delete app data\" you free more space, but the data is gone.
No root. The internet is only used when you ask to update the debloat lists (Settings), and nothing is ever uploaded.
Open \"Backups & restore\", find the most recent backup and tap Restore. If you are not sure which app caused it, use \"Restore everything\".
That\'s normal without root: open Shizuku and tap Start again (Wi-Fi must be on). Your changes are not affected; only new changes need Shizuku.
Yes, if you stick to \"Recommended\" apps and use \"Disable\". Before every change the app saves a backup, and critical system parts are locked so they can never be removed. Everything can be undone.

Android doesn\'t let normal apps turn off other apps. Shizuku is a free helper app that gives Debloater the same rights as a computer connected with a USB cable (ADB), using Wireless debugging. No root and no computer needed.

Turning off frees nothing. Removing with \"Keep app data\" frees almost nothing. Removing with \"Delete app data\" frees the app\'s data (and user apps completely). The app always shows an estimate first and then the space really freed.
It walks through every step (checks, backups, the exact commands) without changing anything, and tells you if something would go wrong. A good habit before any change.

Recommended: bloatware nearly everyone can get rid of.
Safe: no effect on the system, but apps you might still use (for example YouTube).
Extreme: can break features such as payments, updates or the camera. Read the warnings.
Expert and Unsafe (expert mode only): can break important parts of the phone.

Open \"Backups & restore\" on the home screen. Pick a backup and tap Restore, or use \"Restore everything\" to put the phone back the way it was when you first opened Debloater. A factory reset also brings back every system app.

Phones come with many apps you never asked for: ads, tracking, games, duplicate apps. Debloater finds them, tells you which ones are safe to get rid of, and turns them off or removes them, without root.
Does the app need root or the internet?

What is Shizuku and why do I need it?

See exactly what will happen, without changing anything.
Turning off (disabling) is the safest: the app stays but can\'t run.
A backup is made automatically before every change. One tap brings everything back.
Running as %1$s. You\'re ready to go.
Debloater needs Shizuku to turn apps off or remove them. Shizuku gives apps the same rights as a computer connected with a USB cable, without root and without a computer. Follow these steps once:
Shizuku is a free app from the Play Store or GitHub.
Connect to Wi-Fi. Open Settings → About phone and tap \"Build number\" 7 times to unlock Developer options. Then open Developer options and switch on \"Wireless debugging\".
Open Shizuku, choose \"Start via Wireless debugging\", do the one-time pairing it explains, then tap Start. After every restart of the phone you need to tap Start again (unless you have root).
Let Debloater use Shizuku. You will see a pop-up: choose \"Allow all the time\".
Remove the apps you never asked for: ads, tracking and bloatware. Safely, with automatic backups, and without root.
Choose caches from user apps and system apps in one list. App data and accounts are kept.
Stopped. Results may be partial. Completed clears are not undone; an in-flight clear may still finish.
Partial measurements; unavailable sizes are excluded.
Opens Android app settings and presses Clear cache for selected user or system apps, like you would. No Shizuku needed. Unrecognized screens are stopped safely.
Enable the assistant in Android Accessibility settings, return here and confirm clearing. Enabling access does not start cleaning.

The assistant will control Settings for the apps listed below and press only Clear cache. Keep the screen unlocked and avoid touching Settings. Use Cancel on the floating bar to stop. Apps and accounts are kept, but cleared cache cannot be backed up or restored. Unsupported screens or uncertain results stop the batch. Continue?

Optional Accessibility access lets Debloater read visible Android Settings controls and press Storage and Clear cache, only for apps you select and confirm. Screen contents are not saved or sent. A floating Cancel button stays visible while cleaning. You can disable the service in Accessibility settings at any time.
Find folders left by uninstalled apps
Find possible leftovers, review their paths, then move selected folders to recovery. Nothing is selected or deleted automatically.

Current user’s primary storage only: Android/data, Android/obb and Android/media. Installed, disabled and retained package owners are protected. Unrecognized folders and inaccessible areas are skipped.
Shizuku must be running and authorized for scanning and recovery.
Cancel stops after the current bounded file operation. Completed actions are not undone.
Partial scan: some locations or folders could not be checked.
Recovery keeps the files in shared storage and does not free space. Restore them or permanently delete individual records after review.
Restore this recovery folder to its original location? Existing folders are never overwritten or merged. Keep other file operations paused.
Permanently delete these recovery files to free space? They may contain personal files. This cannot be undone and no backup will remain.

These folders may contain personal files. Review every path. Selected folders will move to .DebloaterRecovery in shared storage with their original locations recorded. This is recoverable but does not free space until permanent deletion. Avoid installing or uninstalling apps during this operation. Continue?
Granted by Android at installation; no separate permission prompt. This checks authorization, not network connectivity.
Check official GitHub releases. Downloads use your connection and continue in Android Downloads. Installation requires Android confirmation; no automatic installation.
Update check or download failed. Check your connection and try again.
Download complete. Open the Android download notification or the APK in a file manager to install.
After confirmation, grant Usage Access and try enabling only the cache assistant. Existing Accessibility services are preserved. Android may require manual setup. This does not start cleaning.
